title: Travel Planner

primary_metric: total booked trip cost (theme-park tickets after Gina's discount tier + Priceline-discounted hotel + Gina's 4% agency fee), in USD, checked against the family's fixed $3,950 budget cap

options.B: The Disney Classic Plan -- 2 days at Disneyland, 1 day at LEGOLAND California, 1 beach day, a divided executive suite near the park

modeling_assumptions.text: Every destination in this case treats age 2 (Henrietta) as free admission. San Diego Zoo and Universal Studios Hollywood publish a '2 and under free' / '3 and older pays' cutoff; LEGOLAND's own published cutoff is 'under 2' (age 2 itself would technically pay there). This case applies the more common '2 and under free' cutoff at every destination for one consistent rule.

Universal Studios Hollywood does not sell a single official 3-day ticket product. Plan A's 3 Universal days are modeled as 3 separate 1-Day General Admission tickets purchased together, which qualify for Gina's firm's own 6% '3 or more park-admission days' discount tier per her firm's deal with the park (Background) -- the tier is defined by cumulative admission days booked, not by which ticket product exists on Universal's own retail site.
Hotel nights equal the number of activity days in each plan (Appendix B): Plan A books 5 nights, Plan B books 4 nights -- one night of lodging per activity day.

The Anaheim Marriott Suites nightly rate used for Plan B ($210/night) is the top of a real, cited $102-$210/night range (Appendix F, S6), since Plan B specifically needs the two-room divided executive-suite room type Background describes, not the hotel's cheaper standard room. This is the single largest modeling assumption in the case -- see sensitivity_disclosure below.

deliverables.text: A theme-park ticket cost table for the chosen plan: list price by age category and Gina's discounted price after the correct 2%/6% tier is applied.
A hotel cost breakdown for the chosen plan: nightly rate x nights, then the 8.5% Priceline discount applied.
Gina's 4% agency fee on the chosen plan's combined discounted hotel-plus-ticket total.
A grand total trip cost for the chosen plan, checked against the $3,950 cap, with the margin stated in dollars and as a percent of the cap.
A day-by-day written itinerary with start/end clock times for each block of every activity day and the beach day.
A recommendation comparing both plans' grand totals and percent-of-cap margins from D4.

balance.argument_a: The Wizarding World Plan totals $2,601.65 -- $1,865.66 in discounted tickets (3 Universal days at the 6% tier + 1 Zoo day at the 2% tier), $635.93 in discounted hotel (5 nights x $139 at 8.5% off), and a $100.06 agency fee. That leaves $1,348.35 of headroom under the $3,950 cap (34.14% unused) -- the most budget cushion of the two plans, and it delivers the specific Wizarding World trip Cassy and Elizabeth have discussed for over 2 years, plus a Zoo day that fits Maria, Jimmy Jr., and Elizabeth's shared love of animals and gives Jimmy Jr. (who gets nervous on rides) a lower-thrill day.
balance.argument_b: The Disney Classic Plan totals $2,817.36 -- $1,940.40 in discounted tickets (Disneyland 2-day pass + LEGOLAND at the 2% tier), $768.60 in discounted hotel (4 nights x $210 at 8.5% off), and a $108.36 agency fee. That is $215.71 more than Plan A (8.29% higher), but it still clears the cap with $1,132.64 to spare (28.67% unused), and it buys the specific thing this family's own history points at: Elizabeth's own most treasured childhood memory, a divided executive suite that solves the crib-and-nap logistics Appendix A raises for Henrietta, and a LEGOLAND day that matches Jimmy Jr. and Maria's shared Lego/Ninjago obsession as directly as the Zoo matches their love of animals.
balance.margin_basis: Relative difference between Plan A's and Plan B's grand total trip cost (ticket total after tier discount + hotel total after Priceline discount + 4% agency fee), computed from Appendix C/D's real sourced prices and Appendix E's stated assumptions. See derived{} for the full worked figures.

derived._note: Computed during conversion from Appendix C/D's sourced data and Appendix E's assumptions; case-readiness should re-derive independently, not just trust this block.
derived.twist_alt_convention_note: The twist prices Henrietta's new Universal Day-3 ticket at the standalone 2% single-day tier ($174.28 total extra), not the family's existing 6% 3+-day tier -- an unstated, disclosed convention (see FACILITATOR.md). Under the 6% tier instead, the extra cost is $163.46, not $174.28 -- a small difference that does not change which plan is cheaper or by roughly how much.

sensitivity_disclosure.justification: plan_b_hotel_rate ($210/night) is Appendix E's own disclosed modeling assumption (MA4), the top of a real, cited $102-$210/night range for the Anaheim Marriott Suites (Appendix F, S6) -- no public source fixes an exact rate for a specific divided-suite room type on Jan 12-16, 2026 in advance the way the Zoo's and LEGOLAND's official gate prices are fixed (S3, S4). At -50% (plan_b_hotel_rate down to $105/night, near the bottom of the same cited range), Plan B's grand total drops to exactly $2,417.69, which flips the cheaper plan from A ($2,601.65) to B -- a real, reproducible instability in this case's single largest modeling assumption. plan_a_hotel_rate, all four ticket prices, and the discount/fee percentages all stay stable across the same +/-50% flex range tested for this disclosure.

legacy_conversion_note: Original source: source/Y2/Session 1/Travel Planner/Case Study_ Travel Planner.docx (no separate Guide Notes doc exists for this case -- confirmed by directory listing, only the case study docx is present under that session folder). The binary dilemma used here (3-day Universal/Wizarding World anchor vs. 2-day Disneyland anchor, each a complete itinerary) is taken verbatim in structure from the human-approved lock in cases/_concepts/LEGACY_DILEMMA_LOCKS_2026-08-20.md's 'travel-planner' entry (part of the 3-case 'deep-dive tree pass', HIGH confidence within that pass). The original source's Challenge 3 was open-ended ('a detailed daily itinerary... a detailed budget of all trip costs, including gas, accommodations, theme park ticket costs, food costs, travel snack costs, anything else you feel is important') with zero concrete data given for any of it -- no hotel, no ticket prices, no day-by-day plan. This conversion designs its own concrete day-by-day itinerary skeleton (Appendix B), sources real current ticket and hotel prices (Appendix F), and narrows Challenge 3's scope to the deliverables the sourced data can actually support (tickets, hotel, agency fee, budget-cap check, timed itinerary, recommendation) -- gas and food/snack costs were dropped because Appendix B/the human-approved lock's own 'data to use' list names family composition, the budget cap, the 5 named destinations, the fee structure, and the beach day, but does not name gas or food as case data, and no real per-mile driving distance from Boulder, CO exists in the source to compute a real gas cost against (inventing one would violate the never-fabricate-a-number rule). Every skill this case's real deliverables force (percent-of-a-number, decimal arithmetic, multi-step order of operations, elapsed/clock time, comparison) already has n>0 in readmodel/standards_spine.json, so new_coverage[] is legitimately empty -- this case FORMALIZES pre-existing corpus coverage rather than closing a fresh gap, the same carve-out documented in Family Trip and Gerrymandering's own legacy_conversion_note.
